note: By the criteria as written he passes on starting point and fails on economics, and the economic failure is absolute rather than marginal. He is not deconditioned by any reading — daily planks and stretches, two to four miles most weekdays and five to fifteen miles a day at weekends — and his own framing is squarely good to great: arms, legs and back 'have always been good and relatively defined', 'for my age, I am actually in good form', and the ask is definition in one region. Health is a neglected area rather than a crisis. But he is self-employed with a collapsed client base, gave up his clinic premises when the workload dropped, supplements irregular acting work through an agency, and stated plainly 'I am struggling, in all honesty.' That is a total miss on both the occupation and affordability tests. The wider point this call makes for the ICP is the same one already recorded there — the stated criteria carry no clinical screen, and this prospect is on a waiting list for a knee ligament or tendon replacement, which is the single most relevant fact about whether he can perform the programme and is invisible to all five criteria.
